title: Audit logs & admin activity review - Redwood & Omega Finance
summary: Redwood walked Omega Finance through what is captured in audit logs and admin activity, export/streaming options (S3, syslog, SIEM), retention defaults and custom retention for enterprise, KMS/customer-managed keys, tamper-evidence/append-only storage, and how RBAC/SSO tie into access to logs. Agreed next steps: share sample log schema and S3 export config, schedule SIEM integration tech deep dive, confirm retention SLAs and pricing for extended retention.
topics: what audit logs capture (admin actions, API keys, model deployments)
export options: S3, GCS, syslog, Splunk/Datadog, webhook
retention defaults and extended retention options

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-12
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Maya Kapoor (Omega CISO), Ethan Park (Eng Manager), Sofia Martins (Cloud Sec), Alex Rivera (Compliance)

Auto-generated summary (may be rough):
Redwood reviewed audit logging capabilities, export flows, retention and encryption/KMS options. Customer asked about what exactly is captured, how logs can be exported to their SIEM, tamper-evidence, and long-term retention. Redwood outlined default 90-day retention for hosted and options for enterprise to extend to 1+ years with WORM/archival.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, really appreciate you making time today. main goal is to run through audit logs and admin activity so you can see what omega would get if you move forward with Redwood.
[00:12] Maya: thanks Jordan, yes key things for us are: what is actually logged (like admin changes vs data access), can we stream to Splunk or our SIEM, and what retention options exist. also we need confirmation on customer managed keys for log encryption.
[00:28] Jordan: yep totally, priya will take the deep on the schema and exports, i'll cover high-level compliance and processes.
[00:36] Priya: cool. quick note — transcription might flip a few acronyms, so i'll repeat when needed. starting with scope: our audit logs capture control-plane events and admin activity not the full model inference payloads. so think of: sign-ins, sso events, api key creation/rotation, role changes, model deploys/pin updates, routing policy changes, dataset uploads (metadata), and evaluation runs.
[01:10] Ethan: when you say "model deploys" is that every model version push and also rollback events?
[01:15] Priya: yep, deploys, rollbacks, canary promotions, and who initiated the change. each event includes actor identity, timestamp, IP address, user-agent, resource id, request id/correlation id, and change delta (before/after for config changes). we do not log raw request bodies for inference payloads by default — that can be configured separately but default is to exclude PII and user content.
[01:41] Sofia: is the actor identity tied to SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning? we want log entries to show corporate identity, not just generic service accounts.
[01:50] Priya: yes, we tie to your SAML identity if you enable SSO and SCIM; the logs will show the corporate username and the source (e.g., SSO), and if it's a service token we'll show token id plus associated owner in the metadata.
[02:05] Maya: good. on retention — what's the default? we're required to keep certain logs for 1 year for some audit items.
[02:12] Jordan: for hosted accounts default retention is 90 days for audit logs. for enterprise/dedicated customers we support custom retention: 90 days, 365 days, multi-year archival. extended retention is part of the enterprise package (pricing/commit dependent). we also support WORM-like mode for legal hold scenarios.
[02:35] Alex: when you say "archival" how does the export work — do you push to our S3 or do we pull?
[02:41] Priya: multiple options — push-to-S3 (you give us an IAM role or we use a signed put with SSE-KMS), push to GCS/Azure Blob, syslog/TCP streaming to an on-prem collector, or we can forward to Splunk HEC, Datadog, or another SIEM via a webhook/HEC endpoint. we also support streaming into Kafka if you want to ingest directly.
[03:05] Ethan: is the S3 export encrypted with our KMS? we need customer-managed keys (CMK).
[03:10] Priya: yes — exports support server-side encryption with your KMS (SSE-KMS). we can also do client-side encryption before upload if you prefer. when using our managed export we support customer-managed KMS in AWS, GCP CMEK, and Azure Key Vault. for private deployments you can also bring HSM-backed keys.
[03:30] Sofia: how about tamper-evidence or chain-of-custody — is the log store append-only and signed?
[03:36] Priya: good question. for hosted we store logs in an append-only store with immutable snapshots. we maintain checksums and periodic signed manifests; for enterprise we can provide signed hashes and time-stamped manifests for chain-of-custody. we also support ingesting logs into your own WORM S3 bucket for additional immutability.
[03:58] Maya: auditors sometimes want to see logs of who accessed logs themselves. do you capture admin log access events?
[04:05] Priya: yes — access to audit logs and exports is itself logged. every export request, console view, and API access to the logs has a corresponding audit entry that includes the requesting actor, method, and timestamp. so you get a full breadcrumb trail.
[04:19] Jordan: i'll add that access control is enforced via RBAC — only roles with the proper permission can request exports. SCIM provisioning keeps roles in sync with your directory.
[04:28] Ethan: can we restrict log exports to a particular IP range or to processes running in our VPC?
[04:33] Priya: for private deployment yes. for hosted we support allow-lists at the export endpoint and VPC peering/direct connect options; dedicated customers can use VPC endpoints and restrict sources.
[04:45] Maya: how granular are the events? do you include diff of the config change or just an event that something changed?
[04:52] Priya: we include a change delta for config operations — e.g., routing rule before/after JSON snippet (truncated to avoid PII). for some fields we only store metadata to avoid accidental logging of secrets. we redact secrets and full payloads by default.
[05:08] Sofia: audit hashing — who signs the hashes? do you provide a public key or is that for internal use?
[05:13] Priya: for enterprise customers we can provide signed manifests with a Redwood key and we can also support cross-signing with customer keys in some engagements — this is typically in the private/dedicated deployment contract.
[05:27] Jordan: quick interjection — does omega use Splunk or another SIEM?
[05:31] Maya: we run Splunk and also have a Datadog front for app metrics but security uses Splunk as the source of truth.
[05:37] Priya: great, we have a Splunk HEC connector and can stream JSON events directly. we also have a middleware for batching to reduce overhead.
[05:47] Ethan: any rate limits on log streaming? we need to understand spikes during large ops.
[05:53] Priya: we have backpressure handling — export pipelines buffer and retry. if you stream to Splunk HEC you can size the HEC instances; our default behavior is to batch and back off. we can provide SLA for throughput on dedicated capacity.
[06:07] Alex: what about log completeness / ordering during outages? we need assurances that no events are lost.
[06:13] Priya: events are queued durably; if downstream is down we retain locally for a configurable time window and then retry. for guaranteed delivery you should use our S3 export which gives you object-level storage; for streaming SIEM connectors we provide at-least-once delivery semantics and dedupe ids in the payload so Splunk can dedupe if desired.
[06:33] Maya: are you storing any inference payloads in the logs? that's a big compliance no for some of our data.
[06:39] Priya: by default inference payloads are not included in audit logs. we capture metadata — e.g., request size, duration, model id, but not the user-provided content unless you opt into request logging. if you opt in we have masking features and PII scrubbing.
[06:58] Jordan: i'll reiterate SOC 2/sys controls — our SOC 2 report covers log integrity, retention, and access controls; ISO artifacts available on request.
[07:08] Maya: good, we'll want to see SOC 2 and ISO evidence and any pen test summaries.
[07:13] Jordan: we'll attach those in the follow-up.
[07:18] Priya: more details on the event schema — each entry has: event_type, actor (id/email), actor_source (SSO/API), timestamp, resource_type, resource_id, action, outcome (success/failure), request_id, ip, user_agent, change_delta (if applicable), and tags (e.g., environment, team). we also include a correlation id for multi-step operations.
[07:46] Ethan: can we pipe logs into BigQuery/Snowflake later for analytics?
[07:51] Priya: yes — we can export to a customer bucket and you can run ingestion jobs into BigQuery or Snowflake; some customers also put logs into a raw-events table for retention/analysis.
[08:02] Sofia: what about searchability — do you provide a UI to query audit logs?
[08:07] Priya: yes, Redwood Console has an audit view with filters (actor, event_type, date range, resource). for large volumes we recommend exporting to your SIEM for long-term analytics.
[08:18] Maya: how long do you keep the console UI logs? default is 90 days you said — so beyond that it would be exported?
[08:24] Jordan: console is tied to the retention window; past retention events are archived or deleted based on your entitlement. for enterprise we can keep console-accessible logs for up to 365 days or more depending on the plan.
[08:36] Alex: is there an admin role for only viewing logs and not managing keys or configs?
[08:41] Priya: yes role-based permissions: e.g., audit_viewer, audit_admin, infra_admin, billing_admin. audit_viewer only sees logs and export statuses but cannot create exports or rotate keys. SCIM sync lets you assign groups to these roles.
[08:56] Ethan: curious on implementation detail — are logs written to DB or object storage?
[09:00] Priya: they are written to a dedicated append-only storage optimized for high-write throughput (object-backed) and indexed for query. snapshots of the manifest are taken and signed.
[09:10] Maya: legal e-discovery — if an auditor requests a slice of logs for a given time and user, how fast can you provide that?
[09:17] Jordan: typical turnaround is 48-72 hours for official audit extracts; for enterprise customers we can pre-authorize auditor access or provide direct read-only exports to an auditor S3 bucket to speed that up.
[09:30] Sofia: do you support GDPR/data residency for logs? we need logs to stay in EMEA region.
[09:36] Priya: yes — region-based retention and data residency controls are available for dedicated/regional deployments. for hosted accounts we can route log storage to the region you require (EU region) as part of the onboarding.
[09:50] Alex: question — are admin activity events cryptographically signed per entry or only manifest-level hashes?
[09:56] Priya: currently we provide manifest-level signed hashes and per-chunk checksums. per-entry signing is available as an add-on for private deployments where you bring your own key.
[10:09] Maya: show me a sample log please.
[10:12] Priya: i'll share a redact-ed sample in the follow-up — it will be JSON lines with fields i mentioned. it will show an api_key.create event with timestamp, actor, ip, resource_id, and change_delta showing key metadata.
[10:25] Ethan: about performance — does logging add latency to control-plane ops?
[10:29] Priya: negligible — writes are async. we try to keep control plane latency under SLO by making logging non-blocking. immediate visibility in the console may be near-real time but backend indexing can take a few seconds.
[10:42] Jordan: let's talk about export security — for syslog/TCP we support mTLS and certificate pinning; for webhooks we support HMAC signing of payloads.
[10:53] Sophia: you said webhook HMAC — how do we rotate keys?
[10:56] Priya: you can rotate webhook signing keys from the console or via API; rotation creates a new secret id and older ids are valid for a grace period. rotation events themselves are logged.
[11:08] Alex: do you support legal hold where we can prevent deletion of specific events?
[11:12] Priya: yes — legal hold is supported for enterprise. we mark objects as immutable and they cannot be purged until hold is released.
[11:19] Maya: is there a cost implication for extended retention?
[11:22] Jordan: yes extended retention increases storage costs; we bill enterprise for retention tiers (per GB/month) or via commit for Dedicated. we'll send pricing in the follow-up.
[11:31] Ethan: any gotchas with customer-managed KMS? sometimes cross-account permissions are tricky.
[11:36] Priya: yes you'll need to grant Redwood the ability to put objects with your CMK or provide a role for uploads. we have a docs checklist per cloud — we'll include the exact IAM policy snippets.
[11:48] Maya: do you keep metadata to support policy-based retention? e.g., tag logs by team/project?
[11:53] Priya: yes tags are included in events so you can set lifecycle rules on the exported bucket.
[11:59] Jordan: quick pause — any blockers so far?
[12:02] Maya: no blockers, just want the sample schema and the SOC/ISO docs.
[12:07] Ethan: we'd like to run a short POC: send a week's worth of audit logs to our Splunk instance and verify fields/mapping.
[12:15] Jordan: great, we'll set up a POC. priya will own the integration.
[12:20] Priya: action items noted. i'll include the Splunk HEC connector details and sample HEC config with batching params.
[12:28] Alex: we also need proof that log export requests are logged — can you show that in the POC?
[12:32] Priya: yes that will be part of the test — we'll trigger an export and show the corresponding audit entry.
[12:40] Maya: one more — do you allow retention rules per resource? like keep infra events longer than model deploy logs?
[12:47] Priya: we support resource tagging and retention policies at the bucket level or by event_type via lifecycle policies; per-event retention rules can be configured for enterprise.
[12:58] Jordan: okay wrapping up, we'll compile the docs and get them over.
[13:03] Priya: next steps recap — share schema, share S3 + Splunk config, schedule SIEM deep dive, and provide retention pricing.
[13:11] Maya: thanks everyone.
[13:13] Jordan: thanks — we'll follow up early next week.

(Transcript continues with short clarifying Q&A and recaps)

[35:00] Maya: small nit — for log export to S3 can you include object metadata with team and project tags?
[35:06] Priya: yes, we can include metadata headers and object tags.
[40:00] Ethan: can we have a read-only auditor role with time-limited access?
[40:06] Jordan: yes we support time-limited access tokens for auditors and pre-authorized read-only S3 buckets.
[44:00] Alex: thanks, that covers what compliance asked for.
[44:05] Jordan: great, we will send follow-up items.

End of transcript.
